title: Where I was yesterday
goal: Talk about past states with the past forms of izan and egon, and say when something happened.
bekal: use *nintzen, zinen, zen, ginen, zineten, ziren* for past states
use *nengoen, zeunden, zegoen* for past places and conditions
name past times: *atzo, joan den astean, duela bi urte*

dialogs.title: Elkarrizketa — Asteburua Donostian
dialogs.intro: Monday morning at the euskaltegi. Ainhoa notices Budi arriving with a suntan.

lines.speaker: Ainhoa:
lines.text: Non zeunden asteburuan? Ez zinen hemen egon.
lines.id: Where were you this weekend? You weren't here.
lines.literal: where you-were weekend-in? not you-were here been.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: I was in Donostia, with Nerea.

lines.speaker: Ainhoa:
lines.id: How was it? Was the weather good?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Larunbatean euria ari zuen, baina igandea eguzkitsua zen.
lines.id: On Saturday it rained, but Sunday was sunny.
lines.literal: Saturday-on rain-the doing it-had, but Sunday-the sunny-the was.

lines.speaker: Ainhoa:
lines.id: Did you go to the beach?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Yes, to Zurriola. It was packed with people!

lines.speaker: Ainhoa:
lines.text: Uda da, normala da. Eta zer moduz Donostia?
lines.id: It's summer, that's normal. And how was Donostia?
lines.literal: summer is, normal-the is. and what way-of Donostia?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Oso polita! Baina Bilbo baino garestiagoa zen.
lines.id: Really pretty! But it was more expensive than Bilbo.
lines.literal: very pretty-the! but Bilbo than expensive-er-the was.

lines.speaker: Ainhoa:
lines.id: Ha, ha! You're already a Bilbo local!

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Beharbada... Atzo gauean oso nekatuta nengoen.
lines.id: Maybe... Last night I was really tired.
lines.literal: maybe... yesterday night-in very tired I-was.

lines.speaker: Ainhoa:
lines.text: Normala. Baina orain hemen zaude, klasean.
lines.id: Normal. But now you're here, in class.
lines.literal: normal-the. but now here you-are, class-in.

notes: **Past forms always end in -n.** *Naiz* → *nintze**n***, *da* → *ze**n***, *dago* → *zegoe**n***, *dut* → *nue**n***. The final *n* marks the past for **every** auxiliary, no exceptions. It's one of the neatest rules in the language.

**Euria ari zuen — rain takes the auxiliary ukan.** As mentioned in Unit 10, weather is an exception: *euria ari **du*** (it's raining), *euria ari **zuen*** (it was raining). Basque treats the sky as a doer whose name is never said.

**Bilbotarra — the ending -tar for residents.** *Bilbo* → *bilbotarra*, *Donostia* → *donostiarra*, *Jakarta* → *jakartarra*. The same ending forms nationalities: *indonesiarra*, *japoniarra*. Note the lowercase: unlike English, Basque doesn't capitalize these words.

**Jada — already.** A small word often used to mark a change: *jada bilbotarra zara* (you're already a Bilbo local), *jada berandu da* (it's already late). Another word with the same meaning: *dagoeneko*.

blocks.text: The two verbs split the work just as they do in the present: *izan* for identity and qualities (*ikaslea nintzen* — I was a student), *egon* for place and temporary states (*etxean nengoen* — I was at home).

blocks.title: The most common past sentences
items: *Non zinen atzo?* — Where were you yesterday?
*Oso ondo zegoen.* — It was delicious. (for food)

blocks.text: *Duela* means "ago", and it goes **in front of** the time span: *duela bi urte* (two years ago), *duela hiru egun* (three days ago). English puts "ago" after it — Basque flips the order.

head: Euskara
English
rows: Lehen Jakartan bizi nintzen, orain Bilbon bizi naiz.
I used to live in Jakarta; now I live in Bilbo.
Lehen ez nekien euskaraz, orain pixka bat badakit.
I used to not speak Basque; now I speak a little.
Duela bi urte hasi nintzen ikasten.
I started learning two years ago.

blocks.title: Birth and background
items: *Non jaio zinen?* — Where were you born? *Jakartan jaio nintzen.*
*Noiz jaio zinen?* — When were you born? *Mila bederatziehun eta laurogeita hamaseian.* (1996)
*Non ikasi zenuen?* — Where did you go to school?
*Zenbat urte daramatzazu hemen?* — How long have you been here?
*Duela sei hilabete etorri nintzen.* — I came six months ago.

blocks.text: Verbs that take the auxiliary *izan* — the ones you know from Unit 9 — go into the past just by changing the auxiliary. The verb itself uses its dictionary form, not the *-t(z)en* form.

Notice that the *-t(z)en* form is also used for habits **in the past**: *lehen egunero mendira joaten nintzen* (I used to go to the mountains every day). So *joan nintzen* = "I went (once, that time)", while *joaten nintzen* = "I used to go".

blocks.title: Typical mistakes for English speakers
items: Translating "already" or "have" word for word. Basque needs no extra word: *joan nintzen* already covers "I went" and "I have gone". Add *jada* only when you really want to stress it.
Using the *-t(z)en* form for a single event: ***atzo mendira joaten nintzen*** sounds like "yesterday I used to go to the mountains". The correct form is *atzo mendira joan nintzen*.
Forgetting to change the auxiliary *egon*: ***atzo etxean nago*** is wrong; the correct form is *atzo etxean **nengoen***.
I started learning Basque two years ago.
